sentences: Revolving credit utilization is the most important driver of predicted default, and risk rises sharply once the share of the credit limit in use gets high.
The number of past delinquencies is the second or third most important driver, and having any delinquency raises risk.
Annual income is also among the top three drivers, and higher income lowers predicted risk.
The effect of utilization grows with the number of past delinquencies, so high utilization matters more for applicants with a delinquency history.
Length of credit history lowers risk, but its effect is small.
The data do not settle whether debt-to-income ratio has a weak effect on its own.
Age, months at address, recent inquiries and number of dependents hardly matter for predicted default.
